title: Who’s Asking? Investigating Bias Through the Lens of Disability-Framed Queries in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating how the presence of nine specific disability categories in user queries influences LLMs to make biased or shifted inferences about unrelated demographic attributes, compared to a neutral baseline.
Prompting LLMs to explicitly infer a user's gender (Male or Female) based on the phrasing of a query, and measuring how those predictions skew when disability-related contexts are introduced.
Prompting LLMs to explicitly infer a user's socioeconomic status (Low income or High income) from user queries, comparing prediction distributions between neutral and disability-aware contexts.
Prompting LLMs to infer a user's educational background (Low or High) from user queries to observe whether disability contexts trigger assumptions about educational attainment.
Prompting LLMs to infer a user's cultural background (Western or Non-western) based on user queries, tracking the prediction distributions across neutral and disability-framed queries.
Prompting LLMs to explicitly infer a user's geographic location (Urban or Rural) based on user queries, assessing if disability cues alter the model's assumptions about locality.
